Source: A 57-year-old man presents to the emergency department with several days of malaise, weakness, and night sweats.
Physical exam is notable for a thin man but is otherwise unremarkable.
The patient has a history of diabetes and is followed closely by an endocrinologist.
Otherwise, he has lost 10 pounds over the past month.
His visual acuity is 20/100 in both eyes, though he says that he normally has 20/20 vision.
His gait is mildly ataxic as well, but his neurological exam is otherwise nonfocal.
